panels.description: status is the Python exception class. GraphForbidden points at the app registration's delegated permissions; GraphUnavailable at Graph itself or at this pod's egress. ValidationError, NotFoundError and Advised are caller errors and are not shown, as in Office365McpToolErrors.
panels.title: Tool errors by tool and cause

panels.description: Buckets are hardcoded upstream in unique_mcp/monitoring.py and this chart cannot change them: the top finite bucket is 10s (setup_ops takes duration_buckets for the HTTP histogram only). A Graph request is allowed 30s and a retried one longer, so a quantile sitting exactly on 10 means 'past the last bucket', not 'ten seconds'. Read HTTP request duration for the real tail.
panels.title: Tool call duration

panels.description: Graph operations in each time bucket of at least 15 minutes, by status. Red is a failure. forbidden is a 401 or 403. not_found, cancelled and too_large are answers to the caller.

defaults.noValue: No Graph calls in this range

panels.title: Graph operations by status

panels.description: One observation per tool call, split by the operation it was counted under. operation is a name chosen in code, one per tool — never a Graph URL. graph_client/observability.py says why that is a hard rule.
panels.title: Graph operation rate

panels.description: status is the remedy class from graph_client/errors.py, not the HTTP code: forbidden (consent or permission), throttled, unavailable (Graph or egress), not_found, paging_unending (a collection Graph would not end), too_large (an answer this connector declined to hold), failed, and error for something that is not a Graph failure at all. not_found and too_large are excluded: a caller asking for a chat or a message that is gone got an answer, not an incident, and an answer over this connector's size ceiling is this connector declining correctly rather than failing. forbidden is included — it almost always means the app registration is missing a delegated permission or an admin consent, which is a deployment defect.
panels.title: Graph failures by operation and status

panels.description: End to end, retries and every page of a paged walk included — the Graph work one tool call did, not what one HTTP request took, and not any wait a tool marked as not Microsoft's — a confirmation from a person lands in mcp_call_duration_seconds instead. The top finite bucket is 30s — one Graph request timeout (GraphSettings.request_timeout_seconds), set as a view in office_365_mcp/metrics.py. A quantile pinned on 30 means the call spent Retry-After waits or timed out and was retried; the throttling and status panels say which.
panels.title: Graph operation duration

panels.description: Which tool is the slow one. The top finite bucket is 30s — one Graph request timeout (GraphSettings.request_timeout_seconds), set as a view in office_365_mcp/metrics.py. A quantile pinned on 30 means the call spent Retry-After waits or timed out and was retried; the throttling and status panels say which.
panels.title: Graph p95 duration by operation

panels.description: Graph operations in each time bucket of at least 15 minutes that took 30 to 60 seconds, and more than 60 seconds. The bars are stacked, so the full bar is the number over 30 seconds. Kong and the chat close the request at 60 seconds, so the user gets no answer.

defaults.noValue: No Graph calls in this range

panels.title: Graph operations over 30 and 60 seconds

panels.description: retried=true means the SDK spent its retries and Graph was still throttling. retried=false means Graph asked for a wait past the SDK's ceiling and none was attempted — a quota problem rather than a burst.
panels.title: Throttling rate by operation

panels.description: Pages one paged walk read to answer one call. p99 climbing while the call rate is flat is a filter Graph cannot push down: the walk reads pages to throw them away, and the item scan cap is all that stops it.
panels.title: Pages scanned per walk

panels.description: One observation per Graph call inside a tool, which is the call rate the operation panels do not show. A paged walk is one call here however many pages it read — Pages scanned per walk counts those.
panels.title: Graph call rate by step

panels.description: Which Graph call inside a tool is slow. `operation` is the tool, `step` is the call it made — the panel above says a tool got slower, this one says which of its Graph calls did.
panels.title: Graph p95 duration by step

panels.description: Which Graph call inside a tool is failing, and how. A step counted `forbidden` while its operation is counted `ok` is a tool recovering — teams_read_transcript falling back to an unattributed transcript is the one that does this by design.
panels.title: Graph failures by step and status

panels.description: Buckets are spelled out one page at a time at the low end (office_365_mcp/metrics.py), because nearly every walk reads exactly one. Mass moving off the bottom row is the signal; a walk that gives up on an unending collection lands just past 10.
panels.title: Pages scanned distribution

panels.description: Inbound HTTP, from unique_toolkit's middleware. /, /health, /ready and /metrics are not counted (setup_ops excludes them), so this is MCP and OAuth traffic only — 401s here are the OAuth handshake, not an outage.
panels.title: HTTP request rate by path and status

panels.description: One inbound MCP request end to end, so it contains the tool call and every Graph call that tool made. This is the only one of the three latency histograms whose buckets this service can choose — via setup_ops(duration_buckets=...) in office_365_mcp/app.py — so it is the panel to read for the slow tail. The layout it wants comes from the Graph timeout budget: 30s per request (GraphSettings.request_timeout_seconds) times four attempts (max_retries=3) is 120s, plus Retry-After waits, and a paged walk is several requests — hence buckets at 30, 60, 120 and 300 above prometheus_client's defaults, whose own top finite bucket is 10s. Quantiles sitting on the top bucket mean 'past the last bucket'; read the throttling panel next. Only POST is counted: a GET on /mcp is an event stream that stays open for minutes.
panels.title: HTTP request duration

panels.description: One replica serving 30-second Graph calls: this is the queue depth to watch before adding tools, not CPU.
